items.headline: Anthropic slumps on second day after record-breaking IPO
items.summary: Anthropic shares fell about 9 percent in premarket trading on its second day, dragging down the broader AI sector amid investor concerns about the AI boom. The company holds a market value near $1.27 trillion, or almost $1.8 trillion fully diluted, after raising roughly $120 billion.

items.headline: China's AI firms struggle to match Silicon Valley funding
items.summary: Chinese AI start-ups face soaring model-training costs but cannot raise capital at the scale of US rivals like Anthropic. The financing gap could reshape the global race for AI supremacy.

items.headline: Investors want more despite Anthropic's historic IPO
items.summary: Anthropic pulled off the biggest IPO ever yet shares slid and S&P 500 futures dipped, signaling hurdles for the broader AI industry. The debut valued the company at roughly $1.27 trillion, nearly $1.8 trillion fully diluted.

items.headline: AI trade falters as Anthropic points lower day two
items.summary: Bloomberg reports the market returning to worries about the AI trade after Anthropic's IPO success faded. Broad tech weakness followed the frontier lab's rocky second trading session.

items.headline: How AI is reshaping entry-level science careers
items.summary: Nature examines whether AI automation of coding and basic scientific tasks threatens junior research roles. A free webinar will discuss the technology's impact on skills and job security.

items.headline: Anthropic debut edges past SpaceX as Wall Street test
items.summary: Anthropic notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut, surpassing SpaceX's June listing. The historic IPO capped a turbulent stretch for the AI sector and tested investor appetite.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO prospectus outlines four ways to disrupt science
items.summary: Anthropic aims to cure diseases, accelerate discovery and automate science, but many researchers remain skeptical of its lofty ambitions. The claims featured prominently in its record-breaking offering.

items.headline: Anthropic CEO recommits to pacing AI development at bell
items.summary: At the Nasdaq opening bell, Dario Amodei vowed Anthropic would not bend to business or political pressure and would keep AI 'under human' control. The remarks came as the company completed the largest IPO in history.

items.headline: Anthropic faces political and regulatory scrutiny in Washington
items.summary: Anthropic's prospectus describes AI as cataclysmic and 'existentially' dangerous even as it woos investors. Policymakers have prepared bills to confront those threats, but many remain stuck in Congress.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO prices at $83, raising $107 billion total
items.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share and sold more than 980 million shares for $81.3 billion, plus $26 billion via private placement. The offering paves the way for OpenAI, which has also filed to go public next year.

items.headline: US approved nearly 900,000 AI chip sales to China
items.summary: A House committee says the US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China over six months. Companies sought permission to ship 3.4 million AI chips in the period.

items.headline: Anthropic becomes only true public AI company in US
items.summary: With its Nasdaq listing, Anthropic becomes the only US public company considered a true AI firm until OpenAI's expected debut next year. Investors remain excited but concerned about its path to revenue and profits.

items.headline: AI models ditch hallucinated references and other bad habits
items.summary: A new analysis finds many undesirable large-language-model behaviors dissipate after about 16 months. The findings suggest steady maturation in LLM reliability.

items.headline: $500 billion Nvidia funding deal now in doubt
items.summary: The much-touted $500 billion Nvidia-backed funding deal involving Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock and others has not deployed any capital and is now in question after Jensen Huang's departure. Apollo's chief warns capital for many neoclouds could disappear.

items.headline: Google begins rolling out Gemini 4 Neon frontier model
items.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Neon started rolling out with frontier-level intelligence and fast end-to-end task completion across software engineering, knowledge work and science. It is available to developers, enterprises, consumers and cybersecurity defenders.

items.headline: Economist: self-improving AI models are coming in 2027
items.summary: A Metr report estimates AI capabilities are now growing roughly twice as fast as a year earlier, driven by AI coding tools. Many insiders expect 2027 to be the year AI systems can build their own successors.

items.headline: EU renews push for global AI rules after US midterms
items.summary: The EU is reviving efforts for global AI governance following midterm results that weakened Donald Trump. The move signals renewed transatlantic tension over AI regulation.

items.headline: xAI releases Grok 4.7 frontier model on API
items.summary: xAI's Grok 4.7 is now available via the xAI API with a 500k context window, text and image inputs, and tiered pricing from $2 per 1M input tokens. It supports reasoning effort levels up to xhigh for coding, agentic tasks and knowledge work.

items.headline: OpenAI touts 70% revenue growth and IPO ambitions
items.summary: CFO Sarah Friar said OpenAI's Q3 revenue grew 70 percent with enterprise sales doubling, citing momentum carrying into 2027. She reaffirmed enthusiasm for an eventual IPO as the company's valuation reaches into the trillions.

items.headline: AI startup Mirendil raises $1 billion to accelerate R&D
items.summary: Mirendil, building tools to speed AI research with fewer humans, raised $1 billion in a Series A led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital. The round comes less than six months after a $200 million seed, underscoring aggressive VC deployment into AI.
